From: Alex Li <alex.li@hydrapayments.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@hydrapayments.com>

Subject: Re: P1/P2 on-call rotation gap — mitigation plan & temporary SLA amendment

Hi Ben,

Quick note from overnight: we had a P1 incident (payment routing stall) at 02:42 PDT on 2026-09-12. Our on-call reported an initial contact attempt at ~03:55 (engineer side) and we didn't see the expected triage kickoff from Redwood until 04:30 — by then we had several failed retries. The incident is resolved but the delay caused a short outage to our checkout flow for ~8 minutes.

We understand weekends and shifts are tricky, but this is the second late-night slower-than-expected response in the last three weeks. For our renewal meeting next month this is a concern — we need clarity on on-call coverage and a short-term remediation plan.

Can you confirm:
- What caused the delayed triage for the 02:42 P1?
- Whether Redwood can commit to an interim escalation path / follow-the-sun coverage while you fix the root cause?
- If Redwood can provide a temporary SLA amendment (overnight P1 response window) and a credits proposal to address this impact?

We can loop in procurement if you want formal paperwork; I'm copying them. Appreciate a quick read and proposed next steps today.

Thanks,
Alex Li
Head of Infrastructure
HydraPayments

Attachments: incident_summary_20260912.txt (log excerpt)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@hydrapayments.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: P1/P2 on-call rotation gap — mitigation plan & temporary SLA amendment

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and I'm really sorry you experienced that. I pulled the incident logs and started a quick internal triage; I wanted to respond with immediate actions and a short-term mitigation plan so we can stabilize your coverage while we investigate root cause.

Short answers up front:
- Initial cause: an automated on-call routing failure (edge webhook timeout) coupled with a manual paging fallback delay. We're tracing a race condition in the nighttime routing service that fails to escalate to the backup rotation for ~30–40 minutes in specific states.
- Interim coverage: we can stand-up a temporary follow-the-sun runway for HydraPayments for the next two weeks and a modified overnight P1 response window while we patch the routing service.
- SLA amendment & credits: we can issue a temporary SLA amendment (effective immediately) extending overnight P1 response to 45 minutes for impacted windows and offer a one-time credit equivalent to two days of usage for the event. We'll document formally if procurement requests it.

Proposed immediate actions (today):
1) Put HydraPayments onto our emergency on-call matrix (attached: oncall_gap_matrix.csv) so pages during defined overnight windows route to our escalation tier 2 in EMEA by default.
2) Enable a higher-priority fallback (manual page) if the webhook fails for >5 minutes.
3) Assign Marissa and Laura to own the customer point-of-contact and procurement coordination respectively.
4) Root cause fix: engineering will ship a patched routing service in the next 72 hours; we'll roll it to canary and monitor.

Next steps I propose:
- If that sounds acceptable, we'll prepare a short amendment doc for signatures (I'll include dates and the precise credit amount).
- We can also schedule a 30-minute incident postmortem with your infra team Monday to go over logs and mitigations.

I'm attaching a short mitigation plan PDF with timelines and the on-call matrix. Marissa — can you confirm resource availability for overnight coverage and assist with the temporary manual paging playbook?

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: oncall_gap_matrix.csv; proposed_mitigation_plan.pdf
From: Alex Li <alex.li@hydrapayments.com>

Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: P1/P2 on-call rotation gap — mitigation plan & temporary SLA amendment

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clarity and quick response. The summary looks reasonable and we welcome the follow-the-sun runway while you patch the routing service. A couple of clarifications before procurement signs anything:
- Please confirm effective dates for the temporary amendment (we'd like clear start/end).
- For credits: Procurement has asked for a line-item credit amount rather than a usage-day equivalence so it can be processed in their billing system.
- For the overnight policy: can you confirm time windows (PDT ranges) so we can align internal ops?

If you can send a draft amendment with the dates, credit amount, and exact hours for the overnight window, we can loop in procurement and get signatures. Also yes on a Monday postmortem — 30 minutes is fine.

Alex Li
Head of Infrastructure
HydraPayments
